answers.answer: Not at the next Wake: at that Wake the Exile first checks Usurper victory and then, if still holding the Oathkeeper title, flips it to Usurper. Their first normal Usurper win check is at the start of their following turn's Wake. If round 8 ends first and they still hold the title Usurper-side, the endgame check can award the win then. Losing the title prevents the win; if they later retake it, it resets to Oathkeeper-side and the sequence restarts.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: ‘next Wake check (not yet Usurper), then flip to Usurper, then win at the following Wake’; title loss prevents the win and retaking resets it.

answers.answer: Supremacy matches Conquest; People matches Rebellion; Protection matches Sanctuary; Devotion matches Faith. To win by Vision, an Exile must have the true Vision revealed, meet its goal at Wake, and at least 3 Visions must have been drawn from the world deck by all players combined. For Conquest and Sanctuary, ‘most’ requires strictly more than every other player; ties do not qualify.
answers.evidence: Oathkeeper title and four Oaths table; Visionary victory paragraph.

answers.answer: At the ends of rounds 5, 6, and 7, roll the end die only if the Oathkeeper is the Chancellor or a Citizen. The game ends on 6 in round 5, 5–6 in round 6, or 3–6 in round 7. The Chancellor wins, unless a Citizen meets the Successor goal, in which case that Citizen wins alone. An Exile holding Oathkeeper/Usurper prevents this roll.
answers.evidence: Stable regime: ‘at ends of rounds 5, 6 and 7’; die ranges and Oathkeeper eligibility stated there.

answers.answer: At round 8, check in order: (1) if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper, the Empire wins (Chancellor unless a qualified Citizen Successor wins alone); (2) otherwise an Exile Usurper wins; (3) otherwise a qualifying revealed Exile Vision wins, with simultaneous qualifying Visions prioritized Conquest, Rebellion, Sanctuary, Faith; (4) otherwise Empire wins, with the same Citizen Successor substitution, even if an Exile is Oathkeeper. A Successor goal alone does not end the game; it applies whenever Chancellor would win.
answers.evidence: War exhaustion gives the four ordered checks and Successor rule.

answers.answer: Supremacy: hold more relics and banners than the Chancellor and every other Citizen. People: hold the Darkest Secret. Protection: hold the People's Favor. Devotion: hold the Grand Scepter. A Citizen cannot win with a revealed true Vision or as Usurper; those victory types are for Exiles.
answers.evidence: Oathkeeper table, Citizen Successor goal column; Visionary victory says Citizens/Chancellor cannot win by true Visions or Usurper.

answers.answer: At Wake, if you hold People's Favor, first choose to put 1 favor from your board onto it or return 1 favor from it to a least-full suit bank (choose among tied banks). Never remove its last favor: at 1 you must add if able; if you have no favor, do nothing. If it is already Mob-side, repeat the choice once. After the choice(s), check whether it has at least 6 favor and flip it to Mob if so. Thus reaching 6 at this final check does not cause an additional payment that same Wake.
answers.evidence: Wake step 1: People's Favor choice, last-favor restriction, Mob-side repetition, then 6+ threshold check.

answers.answer: Rest order: (1) return favor on denizens/edifices to suit-matching banks; (2) return secrets on denizens/edifices/relics to your board, then flip your facedown board secrets faceup; (3) Exile/Chancellor refresh Supply to the space shown by their warbands left in personal bank (Chancellor: 18+→6, 11–17→5, 4–10→4, 0–3→3; Exile: 9+→6, 4–8→5, 0–3→4). A Citizen refreshes to the exact Chancellor marker space, including leftmost, not by counting purple warbands. (4) Save unspent Supply by moving the marker one extra space left per unspent Supply, capped at leftmost (7 Supply). (5) Optional Rest powers, each once, in chosen order.
answers.evidence: Rest: mandatory order, steps 1–5, including Citizen marker rule and saved Supply.

answers.answer: Search uses either the world deck or the discard pile for your pawn's region, never both. A discard-pile Search costs 2 Supply. A world-deck Search costs 2 with 0 Visions drawn, 3 with 1–2, or 4 with 3–5; Darkest Secret changes the world-deck cost to 2, while other modifiers still apply. Draw 3 unless the source runs out, a world-deck Vision stops you, or a modifier reduces the draw; you cannot voluntarily stop early. From the world deck draw one at a time; on drawing a Vision announce that one was drawn, stop immediately, and advance Visions Drawn by 1. A Vision from a discard pile does not stop the draw or advance the track. Then discard all but one drawn card before playing that one, or discard the last as well.
answers.evidence: Search section: costs, draw/stop rule, and separate world-deck versus discard-pile Vision treatment.

answers.answer: Discard cards facedown atop the next region's pile in the cycle Cradle→Provinces→Hinterland→Cradle, ordering multiple discards as desired. For hand/adviser discards, use the pile after the region of your pawn (Cradle pawn→Provinces, Provinces→Hinterland, Hinterland→Cradle), never your own region's pile. If discarding a card at a site in a different region, use the cycle after that card's region instead of your pawn's region. Favor on the discarded card immediately returns to its matching bank; secrets on it go to the acting player's board facedown.
answers.evidence: Search—Discard destinations paragraph, including remote-site card rule and resource destinations.

answers.answer: You may have up to 3 advisers total, faceup plus facedown. Before playing over the limit, discard an adviser, subject to locks; if the incoming card changes the limit, check the new limit before playing it, using the lowest of multiple limits. A facedown adviser can be played faceup to a legal destination or discarded later as a minor action, and may be peeked at; facedown cards have no suit, restriction banner, or power, and even Visions or site-only cards may be held facedown. A faceup adviser cannot be discarded at will; it leaves only when a rule permits/requires it. A true Vision revealed by an Exile goes in a separate Revealed Vision space, not an adviser slot. Revealing/playing a replacement true Vision discards the old revealed Vision. Only an Exile can reveal a true Vision; Chancellor/Citizens may hold one facedown but cannot reveal it.
answers.evidence: Search—Adviser and True Vision bullets; Minor actions—play/discard facedown adviser; adviser retention table.

answers.answer: Muster costs 1 Supply: at your pawn's site choose an empty denizen or intact edifice (no favor or secrets on it), place 1 favor on it, and gain 2 warbands from your personal bank to your board (Citizens gain purple). Relics and ruins are ineligible; you need not rule the site and cannot Muster remotely. Trade costs 1 Supply and uses an empty denizen or intact edifice at your pawn's site. Either put 1 secret on it to gain 1 favor plus 1 favor per matching faceup adviser from that card's suit bank, or put 2 favor on it to gain 1 secret per matching faceup adviser from the shared bank. Facedown advisers do not match; with no matching advisers the second option yields zero secrets, though its 2-favor cost remains payable. Gains are limited by available favor/warbands; secrets are unlimited.
answers.evidence: Muster and Trade sections state eligible cards, costs, placements, gains, and no-match case.

answers.answer: Recover costs 1 Supply. You may recover a facedown relic at your site by paying its printed site cost (3 favor to the indicated bank, burn 2 favor, burn 1 secret, or burn 2 secrets); then hold it faceup in your personal bank. You cannot recover a relic held by a player or in the Reliquary. Either banner may be recovered from anywhere, including yourself or the shared bank, by paying strictly more of its resource than it currently has and putting that payment on it. For People's Favor, distribute its old favor one at a time to suit banks, starting at any chosen bank and proceeding through the printed bank order; the previous holder gets none of the old favor. Flip it to normal side if Mob. For Darkest Secret, the new holder takes one old secret and the previous holder takes the rest; recovering from yourself returns all old secrets to you, and from shared bank any remainder stays there. Banner recovery has no seizure penalty.
answers.evidence: Recover section: action cost, relic and banner procedures, old resource distribution, and no seizure penalty.

answers.answer: To recover Darkest Secret from another player, that player's pawn site must contain at least one suited card whose suit matches none of that player's faceup advisers. One such mismatching card is enough, even if other site cards match; a ruin has no suit. If the holder has no faceup advisers but their site has a suited card, it is recoverable. Empty sites and ruin-only sites protect the banner because they have no suited card. This protection does not apply when recovering it from yourself or the shared bank.
answers.evidence: Darkest Secret protection, corrected by official errata: at least one unmatched suited site card; empty/ruin-only and no-adviser cases stated.

answers.answer: A Campaign costs 2 Supply. Choose another player who rules your site or whose pawn is there; if no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. At least one target must be at your pawn's site, and if the defender rules that site you must target it. You may also target any of the defender's sites anywhere on the map, each for 1 defense die. If the defender's pawn is at your site, you may target any of their relics there (printed defense dice), their banners (dice equal to resources on that banner), or their pawn together with their favor (2 dice). A co-located defender's relic target itself meets the required local-target condition.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 1–2: defender eligibility and target selection/local requirement.

answers.answer: Attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in their attacking force; apply modifiers. Defense includes defense dice (including mandatory title bonus: Oathkeeper +1, Usurper +2), plus shields rolled, with each double-symbol doubling shields (multipliers stack), plus warbands at targeted sites and defender board force if defender's pawn is at attacker site or any targeted site. Doubles multiply shields only. Bandits add 1 defense per targeted bandit site. Each attack skull immediately kills one warband from the attacker's own force. Count full swords, plus one attack for each pair of hollow swords; an odd leftover hollow sword adds zero. The attacker may sacrifice surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing must sacrifice exactly enough to win, never excess. Attacker wins only when attack strictly exceeds defense; tie or lower is defender victory.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 2, 4, and 5: dice/force calculation, skulls, sword counting, sacrifice, and strict comparison.

answers.answer: On attacker victory, first the defender kills half the warbands in its defending force, rounded down, returning the rest to board; resolve defeated battle-plan effects. Then attacker may place any number—including zero—of surviving force warbands on any targeted sites; zero leaves them to bandits unless another power applies. Attacker takes all targeted relics and banners. For any seized banner (by any means except Recover), burn 2 of its resources, to a minimum of 1; People's Favor flips to Mob. If pawn-and-favor was targeted, attacker may force defender to travel to a legal chosen site for no Supply, and independently may burn half of defender's board favor rounded down. Respect travel restrictions, with Shrouded Wood overriding the attacker's destination choice when its enemy ruler chooses. Then resolve attacker's victorious battle-plan effects and discard plans marked ‘At end, discard.’ Supremacy title transfer waits until Campaign end.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 6–8 specify defeat casualties before targets, target results, banishment/favor, battle-plan timing, and title timing.

answers.answer: When an Imperial player defends, the Chancellor automatically joins as Ally. Other non-attacking Citizens may join if the defender permits and their pawn is at the attacker's site or a targeted site. The defending side activates relevant modifiers, shares powers as one side, and can use battle plans at Imperial sites and its own advisers (not other players' advisers); each shared plan is used once total by one user, who pays. Allied board warbands contribute defense only when their pawn is at the attacker site or a target. The declared defender chooses order/timing/priority in Ally disagreements. Chancellor chooses which Imperial defending warbands die; site survivors return to Chancellor's board, while Citizen-board survivors stay on their boards. A Citizen attacking Chancellor or another Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign; a Chancellor attacking a Citizen makes that Citizen non-Imperial. An intra-Empire Campaign does not make all Citizens non-Imperial.
answers.evidence: Campaign defender/target steps and Imperial defense subsection state temporary status, allies, shared powers/plans, force and casualty handling.

answers.answer: Base Travel Supply costs by origin→destination region are: Cradle→Cradle 1, Provinces 2, Hinterland 4; Provinces→Cradle 2, Provinces 2, Hinterland 2; Hinterland→Cradle 4, Provinces 2, Hinterland 3. Travel goes to any different site, not necessarily adjacent. If destination is facedown, reveal it and place its printed favor/secrets from shared bank and its printed relics facedown from the relic deck. Pay fixed-number cost first, then other increases/decreases. A power that says ‘spend no Supply’ is the final override, making payment zero even after increases; this covers all Travel, including banishment. Site entry restrictions still apply unless expressly ignored by a power.
answers.evidence: Travel section: region cost table, facedown destination reveal/stocks, and cost order/free Travel override.

answers.answer: During play, the Grand Scepter holder may offer Citizenship to any Exile, including themself, but cannot use Scepter powers on the turn they took it. An offer must promise exactly 1 Reliquary relic; the parties may additionally negotiate binding exchanges of favor, secrets, banners, and non-Reliquary relics, and may allow the recipient to peek at Reliquary relics. On acceptance, the Exile flips to Citizen, replaces all their board/map warbands with purple (if short, they choose which to remove/replace), discards revealed Vision, flips their Usurper title to Oathkeeper, ends their Act if accepting during their own turn, and refreshes to full leftmost Supply. They exchange the promised pieces, and Chancellor gains the newly uncovered mandatory Reliquary modifier. Forced Citizenship uses these conversion steps without a Scepter offer, required relic gift, or invented promised exchange; only actual removal of a Reliquary relic uncovers its modifier.
answers.evidence: Citizenship and exile during play: Grand Scepter, Offer, Acceptance, and Forced Citizenship paragraphs.

answers.answer: Chronicle Oath: if the winner won by a Vision alone, the next Oath matches that Vision; for any other or multiple victory methods, choose any Oath except the current one, and save the goal. Citizenship turnover is a free Chronicle offer by an Exile winner: first flip all Citizen boards, including boxed boards, to Exile; then the winner may offer Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped. Each accepting Exile flips to Citizen and replaces every garrison at every site they rule with exactly one winner-color warband at that site, regardless of its former size. The winner cannot offer themself. Rebuild the world deck from remaining in-play denizens: top stack 10 denizens + 2 random Visions = 12; middle stack 15 denizens + remaining 3 Visions = 18; all remaining denizens below. The aid's ‘12 denizens + 2’ is incorrect; use 10+2, so the top stack is not 14.
answers.evidence: Writing the Chronicle steps 1–2 and 9 state Oath choice, free Citizenship turnover/garrison replacement, and corrected 10+2 top stack.
